newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols pressured by time decay.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols pressured by time decay.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were pressured by time decay ahead of the weekend as underlying markets firmed slightly, recouping a small part of this week's big losses, dealers said.
"It's a really lackluster market," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. "We're just seeing volatilities continue to go lower."

Implied volatility for CBOT June Treasury bond futures options stood at around 9.4 percent in mid-afternoon trading, down from Thursday's 9.5 closing and 9.7 earlier in the day before February's producer price index came out.

Overall PPI fell 0.4 percent in February and the core rate excluding food and energy declined 0.1 percent. Bond prices rallied briefly on the market-friendly numbers but soon faded in the face of an overwhelming bearishness.

Despite growing fears of a Federal Reserve credit tightening at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, the options market appeared more concerned about time decay than event risk, traders noted.
They said the bond market had sold off aggressively in the past week and was likely to be stagnant in the coming week as it awaited the FOMC verdict.

The brokerage trader said such a view was evident in the pricing of April options, which expire next Friday. He noted that the total premium for an at-the-money 109 straddle -- buying a put and a call -- was around one point.
"If you can imagine, a one-week straddle is trading for 64 ticks (64/64)," he said. "The market thinks we're going to stick within a point from 109. We're looking for a very quiet week next week."
Traders said T-bonds had a tendency to gravitate toward the strike prices with highest open interest when front-month options expire, and for the April puts those are 108 and 109.
June futures, which April options will settle against, were up 10/32 at 108-26/32 in mid-afternoon business.
April 108 and 109 puts had open interest of slightly above 27,000 contracts each at end of Thursday's session.
Volatilities at the shorter end of the curve were also easier, in line with a mild bounce in underlying asset prices.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options lost about 0.3 point each at 11.0 and 13.1 percent.
The short-April contract, which has a lot of gamma and is vulunerable to time decay, lost a full point to 18.4 percent.
Short-Aprils are options that expire in April but are priced off June 1997 futures.

At least two houses were seen selling 1,000 contracts each of short-April 93.50 straddles. There were also a few relatively big sellers in green June straddles, which are priced off June 1999 futures.
Traders said those gamma-selling trades were typical when the market became moribund.
"A lot of nickel-and-dime stuff," an investment bank trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "Nothing really surprising."
